currentContext.strengths: Fully integrated CRDMO model spanning discovery, development and commercial-scale manufacturing across large and small molecules, reducing complexity and technology-transfer risk for customers|Long-standing, deep strategic partnerships with global majors, including the extension of the Bristol Myers Squibb (BMS) Dedicated Center collaboration through 2035|Scale of scientific talent - over 5,700 scientists and 8,300 total workforce - supporting speed, data security and world-class manufacturing|Emerging dual-continent manufacturing footprint (India plus the U.S. Bayview facility) supporting supply continuity and global delivery|India cost competitiveness, strong scientific talent base and improving regulatory track record positioning it to benefit from supply-chain diversification (China+1) and the U.S. BIOSECURE Act|Revenue visibility and predictable cash flows from long-term (5+ year) Dedicated R&D Center partnerships|Diversified services portfolio and durable customer relationships across ~400 global customers cited as supporting resilient underlying growth despite a large single-collaboration destocking headwind in FY26
currentContext.strategies: Extend and expand the Dedicated R&D Centers model - continuing to strengthen existing long-term client partnerships (which provide revenue visibility and predictable cash flows) while exploring opportunities to expand engagement with these clients beyond the dedicated center model|Deepen presence in emerging high-growth modalities - peptides and antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) - viewed as areas of increasing customer importance requiring scientific depth and integrated execution|Expand and strengthen manufacturing platforms across small molecule (complex formulations, commercial-scale production) and biologics (development, manufacturing and clinical supply capabilities), including continued build-out of the U.S. Bayview facility alongside India expansion|Shift capital allocation emphasis from capacity creation toward improving asset utilization, strengthening productivity, and enhancing return on invested capital|Continue investment in digitization, automation and process optimization to improve turnaround times, productivity and scalability of the expanded asset base|Maintain disciplined capital allocation and balance sheet strength (net cash position) to preserve flexibility for growth priorities amid a variable operating environment|Leadership transition to Siddharth Mittal as Managing Director & CEO following Peter Bains stepping down at end of June 2026, with continuity of strategic direction expected|In Research Services, continue enhancing and expanding service offerings in FY27 through investments in technical talent and enabling technologies, with a focus on customer centricity, process automation, and a reduced cost base
currentContext.expansion: Large Molecule: Unit-3 in Bengaluru (acquired from Stelis Biopharma) was operationalised and successfully licensed in Q1FY26, now fully functional for multi-product clinical and commercial biologics manufacturing on single-use technology platforms, and secured a manufacturing test license for sterile injectables following a successful regulatory inspection. Syngene completed the acquisition of its first US-based biologics site (Bayview, Maryland); the ongoing modification and integration of this site are progressing as planned, and once fully integrated the US site will augment Syngene's total global single-use bioreactor capacity to 50,000L, establishing a dual-continent (India + US) supply chain. Preparations are in progress toward Bayview's operationalization in FY27. A dedicated GMP bioconjugation/conjugation suite was launched at Unit-3 in FY26, enabling fully integrated ADC services from discovery to manufacturing, as part of a broader CDMO capacity-expansion plan continuing into the subsequent period. n-1 perfusion capabilities were successfully demonstrated at lab scale in the Process Development laboratory, and approval was obtained to demonstrate the technology at large scale, with execution planned in subsequent quarters. Small Molecule: a new commercial-scale facility for liquid-filled hard gelatin capsules was commissioned, strengthening the oral solid dosage platform. Quality capability additions included a new Bioassay laboratory at Unit 3 (Biologics QC) and phased renovation of an existing Small Molecule QC facility to increase analytical throughput. On IT infrastructure, the Company initiated a SAP S/4HANA RISE transformation program (business process re-engineering completed, implementation progressing toward an April 2027 go-live) and integrated the Baltimore Bayview site into its digital/IT infrastructure. The Company is also exploring further capacity expansion and evaluating strategic entry into high-value segments such as ADCs and oligonucleotides.

risks.note: Long-term scientific programmes and multi-year collaborations are typical in the CRDMO industry, creating dependence on revenue from a limited number of clients; the Board flagged this alongside the FY26 impact of destocking at the Company's largest single manufacturing collaboration.
Fast-shifting geopolitical currents and global supply chain volatility are an ongoing challenge; management is responding with a dual-sourcing strategy and expanded local raw-materials ecosystem.

Compliance is integral to client trust and licence-to-operate in the CRDMO sector; laws and responsibilities are mapped across functions via Synpliance, the Company's digital compliance management platform.

Accelerating digitalisation raises the stakes of protecting sensitive scientific, client and operational data; managed via a multi-layered cybersecurity framework aligned with ISO 27001, continuous monitoring and periodic independent audits.

Syngene's capability base is anchored in a highly skilled scientist workforce; availability of skilled talent for future-ready roles is treated as a distinct enterprise risk requiring structured workforce planning and retention programmes.

Rapid advances in science and technology continuously raise client expectations in the CRDMO industry, making sustained investment in scientific/technology capability central to remaining competitive.
AI is rapidly emerging as a key competitive enabler in life sciences; timely, responsible adoption is flagged as essential to remain competitive and meet evolving client expectations.
Uninterrupted scientific delivery is critical to client trust in the CRDMO sector; managed through business-impact assessments, continuity/disaster-recovery plans and regular preparedness drills.

one-line thesis: Syngene delivered robust Q2FY23 growth driven by strong demand in US/EU discovery and development services, with biologics manufacturing set to become a major revenue driver from FY24. The company is strategically expanding capacity and leveraging its SynVent platform to capture integrated drug discovery contracts, while maintaining healthy margins despite rupee volatility and rising input costs.
financial scorecard: rev: +26% YoY; EBITDA: +22% YoY; PAT: +11% YoY; orderbook: strong; netdebt: low (no debt mentioned, capex funded by cash)
guidance: Full-year revenue growth guidance of high teens (15-19%); EBITDA margin guidance of ~30%; PAT growth expected in single digits due to higher tax rate and Remdesivir base effect.
order book & pipeline: Strong demand across all divisions; increased collaborations with emerging biopharma; 18 active SynVent integrated programs; no order book decline noted; visibility supported by long-term Zoetis contract starting FY24.
segment / subsidiary detail: Discovery Services: 26% revenue growth; strongest demand in discovery chemistry; SynVent platform now has 18 integrated programs; Dedicated Centers: operationalized new translational lab for BMS; Development Services: growth from repeat clients and emerging biotechs; Biologics Manufacturing: Zoetis Librela drug substance PPQ batches completed; regulatory inspections pending; commercial manufacturing expected in Q4FY23; Small Molecule Manufacturing: Mangalore plant on track for regulatory approvals in H2FY24.
growth verticals / optionality: SynVent platform scaling to capture integrated drug discovery contracts; biologics manufacturing ramp-up with Zoetis (FY24+) and potential future clients; Mangalore small molecule plant (H2FY24) adding capacity; expanding university partnerships for talent and innovation pipeline.
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin normalized to 28.9% (ex-hedge) vs 28.6% YoY; material costs at 25.9% of revenue (below 27% guidance, will rise with manufacturing mix); staff costs down to 28.4% (from 31%) due to efficiency; power/utility costs up 39% due to fuel prices; renewable energy investments mitigating inflationary pressure.
capex / expansion: US$30M in H1FY23 (30% of full-year US$100M guidance); 50% allocated to research services, 30% to biologics, 20% to infrastructure, safety, digitization; remaining US$70M to be spent in H2FY23.
capital allocation: Capex focused on strategic capacity expansion (biologics, discovery); no dividends or buybacks mentioned; debt levels low; interest rate swaps hedge FX and rate risk; cash flow used to fund growth, not leverage.
risks & watch-items: Rupee depreciation impacting EBITDA margins (hedge losses of Rs.19cr in Q2); rising energy/fuel costs; tax rate increase to 21.5% (gradually to 25% by FY26); potential funding crunch for emerging biotechs (mitigated by credit policy); regulatory delays for Mangalore or Zoetis plant; geopolitical disruptions (though deemed minimal impact).
management quality / tone: Confident and upbeat; emphasized strong underlying demand, successful execution, and strategic positioning; dismissed concerns over GCCs in India as non-threatening; viewed tightening biotech funding as a positive for Syngene’s cost arbitrage model; clear focus on long-term capacity build-out and margin stability.
non-obvious takeaways: Despite rupee depreciation boosting top-line revenue, hedge losses offset bottom-line gains — a hidden drag on margins not immediately apparent from headline revenue growth; SynVent’s integrated model represents a structural shift from transactional CRO to value-chain-as-a-service, creating higher-margin, sticky client relationships; tax rate increase is P&L-only (no cash impact till FY25-26 due to MAT credits).

ANTHEM/COHANCE/NEULANDLAB/SYNGENE-tier on CRDMO (peptides/ADCs/oligos); DIVISLAB/LAURUSLABS on peptide CDMO; AKUMS/INNOVACAP/RUBICON on formulation CDMO; AARTIPHARM/SUPRIYA/AARTIDRUGS/SOLARA on APIs; SIGACHI/NATCAPSUQ/VIDHIING on excipients.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Syngene is an integrated research, development, and manufacturing services company serving global pharmaceutical, biotechnology, nutrition, animal health, consumer goods, and specialty chemical customers, operating as both a Contract Research Organization (CRO) and a Contract Development and Manufacturing Organization (CDMO) for large and small molecules. It employs over 8,300 people including 5,700+ scientists across more than 3 Mn sq. ft of specialized discovery, development and manufacturing facilities in India and the U.S., and works with around 400 global customers including biotech innovators and multinationals such as BMS, GSK, Zoetis and Merck KGaA.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Global CRO market (pre-clinical + clinical) valued at ~USD 84 bn in 2024, expected to grow at ~11% CAGR to ~USD 140 bn by 2029 (Frost & Sullivan), driven by rising R&D activity, outsourcing demand and improving technological capability
- Structural long-term drivers intact - cost optimization imperatives, increasing scientific complexity, supply chain diversification, growth in new modalities, and adoption of advanced technologies - continue to support sustained CRDMO demand despite near-term softness
- Near-term demand environment remains mixed/uneven: cautious global macro conditions, evolving tariffs, and cautious capital allocation by large pharma and biotech are producing slower decision cycles and smaller work packages
- Biotech funding recovered in H2 2025 (back-ended, strong Q4 momentum) but the translation into CRO revenue typically lags 6-12 months, so CRO demand is expected to stay soft in early 2026 with gradual recovery later in the year
- China+1 supply-chain diversification and the U.S. BIOSECURE Act (enacted December 2025) are structural tailwinds for India-based CRDMOs, but realization is expected to be gradual and play out over a multi-year horizon
- Competitive intensity continues to increase notably in China, Asia and India
- Pharma innovators increasingly prefer integrated, end-to-end CRDMO partners to reduce complexity, timelines and technology-transfer risk across the value chain
- Growing adoption of AI/digital technologies across discovery, manufacturing and quality systems is beginning to reshape the CRDMO landscape and is expected to be a productivity differentiator over time
- FY26 revenue growth (3% YoY, consolidated Rs 37,387 Mn) and margin (25% Operating EBITDA) were impacted by destocking at the Company's largest single manufacturing collaboration; stripping this out, underlying growth was resilient at mid-to-high single digits led by Research Services momentum
- Near-term outlook (FY27 H1) expected to remain measured, with the destocking-related biologics program impact continuing into the first half of the next fiscal year before a healthy pipeline and sustained customer engagement are expected to translate into improved growth and operating leverage
- Large Molecule division saw a growing pipeline of opportunities with increasing client engagement and sustained interest in its integrated services model
- Increasing traction in Process Research and Development (PRD) engagements in the Small Molecule division, which serve as an entry point for deeper collaboration and progression into subsequent development stages
- Repeat business from Development Services in the Small Molecule division remained strong and consistent with historical trends, reflecting long-term client partnerships

margins.body: EBITDA margin normalized to 28.9% (ex-hedge) vs 28.6% YoY; material costs at 25.9% of revenue (below 27% guidance, will rise with manufacturing mix); staff costs down to 28.4% (from 31%) due to efficiency; power/utility costs up 39% due to fuel prices; renewable energy investments mitigating inflationary pressure.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Capex focused on strategic capacity expansion (biologics, discovery); no dividends or buybacks mentioned; debt levels low; interest rate swaps hedge FX and rate risk; cash flow used to fund growth, not leverage.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Large Molecule: Unit-3 in Bengaluru (acquired from Stelis Biopharma) was operationalised and successfully licensed in Q1FY26, now fully functional for multi-product clinical and commercial biologics manufacturing on single-use technology platforms, and secured a manufacturing test license for sterile injectables following a successful regulatory inspection. Syngene completed the acquisition of its first US-based biologics site (Bayview, Maryland); the ongoing modification and integration of this site are progressing as planned, and once fully integrated the US site will augment Syngene's total global single-use bioreactor capacity to 50,000L, establishing a dual-continent (India + US) supply chain. Preparations are in progress toward Bayview's operationalization in FY27. A dedicated GMP bioconjugation/conjugation suite was launched at Unit-3 in FY26, enabling fully integrated ADC services from discovery to manufacturing, as part of a broader CDMO capacity-expansion plan continuing into the subsequent period. n-1 perfusion capabilities were successfully demonstrated at lab scale in the Process Development laboratory, and approval was obtained to demonstrate the technology at large scale, with execution planned in subsequent quarters. Small Molecule: a new commercial-scale facility for liquid-filled hard gelatin capsules was commissioned, strengthening the oral solid dosage platform. Quality capability additions included a new Bioassay laboratory at Unit 3 (Biologics QC) and phased renovation of an existing Small Molecule QC facility to increase analytical throughput. On IT infrastructure, the Company initiated a SAP S/4HANA RISE transformation program (business process re-engineering completed, implementation progressing toward an April 2027 go-live) and integrated the Baltimore Bayview site into its digital/IT infrastructure. The Company is also exploring further capacity expansion and evaluating strategic entry into high-value segments such as ADCs and oligonucleotides.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident and upbeat; emphasized strong underlying demand, successful execution, and strategic positioning; dismissed concerns over GCCs in India as non-threatening; viewed tightening biotech funding as a positive for Syngene’s cost arbitrage model; clear focus on long-term capacity build-out and margin stability.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Fully integrated CRDMO model spanning discovery, development and commercial-scale manufacturing across large and small molecules, reducing complexity and technology-transfer risk for customers
- Long-standing, deep strategic partnerships with global majors, including the extension of the Bristol Myers Squibb (BMS) Dedicated Center collaboration through 2035
- Scale of scientific talent - over 5,700 scientists and 8,300 total workforce - supporting speed, data security and world-class manufacturing
- Emerging dual-continent manufacturing footprint (India plus the U.S. Bayview facility) supporting supply continuity and global delivery
- India cost competitiveness, strong scientific talent base and improving regulatory track record positioning it to benefit from supply-chain diversification (China+1) and the U.S. BIOSECURE Act
- Revenue visibility and predictable cash flows from long-term (5+ year) Dedicated R&D Center partnerships
- Diversified services portfolio and durable customer relationships across ~400 global customers cited as supporting resilient underlying growth despite a large single-collaboration destocking headwind in FY26

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Rupee depreciation impacting EBITDA margins (hedge losses of Rs.19cr in Q2); rising energy/fuel costs; tax rate increase to 21.5% (gradually to 25% by FY26); potential funding crunch for emerging biotechs (mitigated by credit policy); regulatory delays for Mangalore or Zoetis plant; geopolitical disruptions (though deemed minimal impact).

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Despite rupee depreciation boosting top-line revenue, hedge losses offset bottom-line gains — a hidden drag on margins not immediately apparent from headline revenue growth; SynVent’s integrated model represents a structural shift from transactional CRO to value-chain-as-a-service, creating higher-margin, sticky client relationships; tax rate increase is P&L-only (no cash impact till FY25-26 due to MAT credits).

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Extend and expand the Dedicated R&D Centers model - continuing to strengthen existing long-term client partnerships (which provide revenue visibility and predictable cash flows) while exploring opportunities to expand engagement with these clients beyond the dedicated center model
- Deepen presence in emerging high-growth modalities - peptides and antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) - viewed as areas of increasing customer importance requiring scientific depth and integrated execution
- Expand and strengthen manufacturing platforms across small molecule (complex formulations, commercial-scale …

challenges.body:

> The challenges management discussed — rising fuel/energy costs (power & utility up 39% on natural gas / high-speed diesel), rupee depreciation & hedge losses (Rs.19cr), the gradual SEZ-exit tax-rate step-up, tightening US biotech funding, and MNC captive R&D centers (GCCs) in India (Baxter, Herbalife, Pfizer, Merck) — either eat into Syngene's own P&L (loser = self) or name only foreign / non-tradeable entities. other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Leadership] Siddharth Mittal assumed charge as Managing Director & CEO on July 1, 2026.
- [Partnership] Signed an MoU with BRIC-Translational Health Science and Technology Institute (THSTI), an institute under the Biotechnology Research Innovation Council, Department of Biotechnology, Government of India — a joint operational partnership for early and late-phase clinical development, translational research and bioanalytical sciences.
- [Guidance] "While we expect a degrowth in the first half of the fiscal year, business momentum is expected to improve in the second half, resulting in single-digit revenue degrowth in rupee terms for the full year and EBITDA margins in the mid-20s".
- [Group structure] Syngene is an operationally independent publicly listed subsidiary of Biocon Limited (founded 1978), which has majority holding in key operating entities including Syngene.
- [Risk governance] Enterprise-wide risk management framework with four accountability layers — Operating Unit/Enabling Function Heads, Risk Management Committee, Executive Committee and Board of Directors.
